p: Lee orders the retreat to begin on July 4. Imboden's cavalry will escort the enormous wagon train of wounded — 17 miles long. Lee takes full responsibility for the defeat.
Imboden described Lee at this moment: 'I never saw a man so agitated in my life' — pacing back and forth, saying over and over 'Too bad. Too bad. Oh, too bad.'

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)

p: Rain begins. Both armies exhausted. The Battle of Gettysburg is effectively over. Union casualties: approximately 23,000. Confederate casualties: approximately 28,000. Total: ~51,000 in three days.

END OF THE BATTLE. Total Confederate losses approximately 37% of the army engaged. Total Union losses approximately 25%. The Confederate Army of Northern Virginia will never again mount a strategic offensive into the North. The High Water Mark of the Confederacy has passed.

Gettysburg, combined with Vicksburg's fall on July 4, marks the turning point of the Civil War. The Confederacy would fight on for nearly two more years but the strategic initiative passed permanently to the Union.

p: Hood wounded — Law assumes division. Hood's arm was permanently paralyzed. He continued to serve but never recovered full use of it. Reported time: July 2 ~4:15pm.

p: Armistead mortally wounded beyond The Angle. Armistead fell among Union soldiers beyond the wall. He asked for Hancock to be brought to him. He died July 5 in a Union field hospital. Reported time: July 3 ~3:30pm.
